article.title: Calibration vs. Ranking: A Model Can Order Customers Well and Still Give Bad Probabilities
article.why: Deep Dive connecting model evaluation to targeting and business decisions.

paragraphs.en:
A predictive model can be useful in two very different ways. It can rank customers from more likely to less likely to respond, or it can estimate the actual probability that each customer will respond. These tasks sound similar, but they are not the same. A model may be excellent at ranking while producing probabilities that are systematically too high or too low.

Suppose an insurance campaign model assigns Customer A a score of 0.80 and Customer B a score of 0.60. If A truly has a higher response propensity than B, the ranking is correct. For a campaign that simply sends messages to the top 100,000 customers, ranking quality may be the main concern. Metrics such as AUC are often used to evaluate how well a model separates positive and negative cases across thresholds.

Now imagine that the business interprets 0.80 as an 80 percent chance of response. That interpretation requires calibration. A well-calibrated model should make probabilities that correspond reasonably to observed frequencies. Among many cases assigned a probability near 0.20, roughly 20 percent should experience the event, subject to sampling variation and stable conditions. If only 2 percent respond, the ranking could still be useful, but the numerical probability is badly calibrated.

This distinction becomes important when probabilities enter financial decisions. Suppose a company sends an offer only when expected profit is positive. Expected value might depend on response probability, expected margin, contact cost, and risk. If the probability is inflated by a factor of ten, the company may contact many customers whose expected value is actually negative. A good ranking cannot automatically rescue a decision rule that treats uncalibrated scores as literal probabilities.

Extreme class imbalance makes the issue more visible. In a dataset where only one in a thousand customers converts, a model can rank the rare positives well while its raw scores bear little resemblance to real conversion rates. Sampling strategies can also distort probabilities. If training data deliberately contains one positive for every ten negatives even though production has one positive for every thousand negatives, a model trained on that sample may require adjustment before its probabilities are interpreted in the real population.

Calibration can be evaluated with reliability plots, calibration curves, Brier scores, and grouped comparisons between predicted and observed rates. Methods such as Platt scaling or isotonic regression can sometimes improve probability estimates using suitable validation data. However, calibration is not permanent. If customer behavior, campaign design, eligibility rules, or the base rate changes, previously calibrated probabilities may drift.

The business question should determine the evaluation method. If the goal is to prioritize a fixed number of customers, ranking metrics, lift, precision at k, and decile performance may be especially relevant. If the goal is to estimate expected revenue, set a probability threshold, price risk, or compare economic value, calibration becomes much more important. In many real projects, both matter.

A useful reporting habit is to avoid calling every model output a 'probability.' Use 'score' when the value is primarily for ranking unless calibration has been demonstrated. Then show ranking performance and calibration performance separately. This prevents stakeholders from assuming more meaning than the model has earned. The central lesson is that ordering cases correctly and estimating their absolute likelihood are distinct statistical achievements, and a model should be judged according to the decision it is supposed to support.
paragraphs.zh: 重點翻譯：ranking 與 calibration 是不同能力。模型可以把高風險／高轉換者排在前面，因此 AUC、lift 很好，但 0.8 不一定真的代表 80% 機率。若只是挑 top-N，ranking 可能已足夠；若要算 expected value、設定 probability threshold 或做風險定價，就必須重視 calibration。極度不均衡與重抽樣尤其容易讓 raw score 與真實 base rate 脫節。
paragraphs.ja: 要点訳：ranking性能とcalibrationは別物である。上位顧客を正しく並べられても、0.8というscoreが80%の発生確率を意味するとは限らない。top-N配信ならrankingが中心だが、期待値計算や確率thresholdに使う場合はcalibrationが重要になる。不均衡データやsamplingでは特に注意が必要。

vocabulary.usage: Calibration checks whether predicted probabilities match observed frequencies.
Ranking quality matters when selecting the highest-scoring customers.
Probabilities may be systematically too high even with good ranking.
A response propensity score can be used to order customers.
Financial decisions may depend on a probability threshold.
Inflated probabilities can make negative-value contacts appear profitable.
Extreme class imbalance complicates probability interpretation.
Reliability plots compare predicted and observed event rates.

vocabulary.zh: 等張／單調的（校準法名稱）
vocabulary.usage: Isotonic regression is one method used for calibration.
Calibration can drift when the base rate changes.
Do not treat a raw score as a literal probability without evidence.
Absolute likelihood estimation is distinct from relative ordering.

business.term: Use ranking metrics for prioritization and calibration metrics for probability-based decisions.
business.explanation: 排序型決策與機率型決策要使用不同評估指標。

business.term: Call the output a score unless probability calibration has been demonstrated.
business.explanation: 未證實 calibration 前，將輸出稱為 score 比 probability 更精確。
